title: Example 128 (B9, JBMC, violation) with its witness as typed calls of both versions
description: jvmcontract's equivalence and prove outcomes now keep each counterexample's witness as data (the second half of step 3b of llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md): typed inputs with exact values (a long as a decimal string, a float or double as Java's toString), the patched version's call (class, class file, descriptor, static or not, the receiver as a record of its components, each argument naming the input it came from) and for a regression proof the previous version's call, whose arguments under previousArguments name the expression that computed them. build.py records it as counterexamples[].witness, with each class file's SHA-256 as built. The verdict and every other field must be unchanged; the counterexample must gain a witness that validates against the schema. 128's new version is a record's method and its previous version static, called with expressions over the components: witness.call must have the receiver Batch[start, size] and previousCall the static offsetToCommit (JII)J with arguments from this.start, this.size and failedIndex, both class files with a digest.
expected: example 128 gives its expected verdict, violation: build.py prints 'as expected' and exits 0

resources.notes: a JBMC violation on a record method, 0.5 s; the rest is javac
